rulebaseSources: Kenyan Labour Law & Film Production Regulations

special.nightToDay: 12-hour minimum for all categories when transitioning from a night shoot (wrap after 8 PM) to a day shoot (call before 8 AM)

mealBreakRequirements.firstMeal: Must be provided within 6 hours of call time
mealBreakRequirements.secondMeal: Must be provided within 12 hours of call time
mealBreakRequirements.childPerformers: Maximum 3 hours between meals, 45 minutes minimum duration
mealBreakRequirements.penalties: Applicable for late or missed meals, calculated per violation

premiums.nightPremium: 25% on base hourly rate for work between 8 PM - 6 AM
premiums.saturdayPremium: 50% on base hourly rate (or time and a half)
premiums.sundayPremium: 100% on base hourly rate (or double time)

onSetRequirements.tutor: Mandatory if child is missing school
onSetRequirements.welfareOfficer: Mandatory for 3 or more children on set
onSetRequirements.guardian: Parent/guardian must be on set at all times
onSetRequirements.breaks: Mandatory 15-minute break for every hour of work

animalWelfareRequirements.approvals: RSPCA approval required for all animal sequences
animalWelfareRequirements.personnel: Certified veterinarian on site during filming; Handler must have Level 3 certification
animalWelfareRequirements.workSchedule: Minimum 2-hour rest period every 4 hours of work
animalWelfareRequirements.safety: Minimum 50 meters safety distance for dangerous animals

personnel.coordinator: IATSE-certified stunt coordinator required for all planning and execution
personnel.safetyOfficer: Mandatory on set for all stunt sequences
personnel.paramedic: Required on standby for high-risk stunts

procedures.rehearsals: Minimum of 3 full rehearsals required before filming a stunt
procedures.fireStunts: Limited to 15-second maximum exposure per take

workPermits.validity: 6 months maximum for temporary employment permits
workPermits.specialApproval: Labor office approval required for all weekend and night work

onSiteRequirements.insurance: Comprehensive medical insurance and emergency evacuation plans required for all foreign crew/cast
onSiteRequirements.communication: Satellite communication equipment mandatory for remote locations
onSiteRequirements.localSupport: Local fixer and security arrangements required

hardConstraints.description: Child performers must have a minimum 16-hour rest period between work days.
hardConstraints.violation: Legal violation, production halt, potential fines and license revocation.

hardConstraints.description: Minimum turnaround times (10/11/12 hours based on category) must be respected for all cast and crew.
hardConstraints.violation: Forced call (violates union rules), results in severe financial penalties (e.g., day's pay per hour of violation) and safety risks.

hardConstraints.description: A meal break must be provided no later than 6 hours after call time.
hardConstraints.violation: Union violation triggering escalating financial penalties for every 30-minute delay.

hardConstraints.description: Daily and weekly work hour limits for child performers, based on age, cannot be exceeded.
hardConstraints.violation: Severe legal violation, immediate work stoppage, fines, and potential criminal charges.

hardConstraints.description: An IATSE-certified stunt coordinator and a safety officer must be present for all stunt sequences.
hardConstraints.violation: Gross negligence, invalidates production insurance, severe safety and legal liability.

hardConstraints.description: Animal work is prohibited in temperatures below 10°C or above 32°C.
hardConstraints.violation: Violation of animal welfare laws, RSPCA can halt production, results in fines and negative publicity.

hardConstraints.description: All non-local cast and crew must have a valid Kenyan work permit before commencing any work.
hardConstraints.violation: Illegal employment, results in deportation, fines, and potential ban on future filming in the country.

softConstraints.description: Limit consecutive work days to a maximum of 6 before a mandatory 24-hour rest day.
softConstraints.violation: Working a 7th consecutive day incurs significant overtime/premium pay penalties and increases crew fatigue.
softConstraints.penalty: Typically 1.5x or 2x daily rate for the 7th day, depending on union agreement.

softConstraints.description: Avoid scheduling on weekends (Saturday/Sunday) to prevent premium pay.
softConstraints.violation: Incurs significant budget increases due to premium pay rates.
softConstraints.penalty: 50% premium for Saturday work, 100% premium for Sunday work.

softConstraints.description: Schedule scenes at the same location consecutively to minimize company move time and costs.
softConstraints.violation: Increased transportation costs, lost shooting time due to company moves, potential for location re-booking fees.
softConstraints.penalty: Non-financial penalty related to schedule inefficiency and budget overruns.

mealPenalties.description: Calculated in 30-minute increments for delays past the 6-hour mark.
mealPenalties.rate_0_to_30_mins_late: 1.5x the employee's hourly rate for that 30-minute period.
mealPenalties.rate_past_12.5_hours: Penalty rate increases to 2x hourly rate.

overtimePenalties.description: Calculated based on total hours worked in a day.
overtimePenalties.rates: Time and a half (1.5x), Double Time (2x), and Golden Time (e.g., 3x or negotiated flat rate) as per union rules.

turnaroundPenalties.description: A forced call (violating turnaround) is a severe infraction.
turnaroundPenalties.penalty: Typically, the employee receives one full day's pay for each hour or fraction thereof that the rest period is invaded.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Initiate Kenyan work permit applications for all non-local cast and crew immediately. The 21-day minimum processing time is a critical path dependency.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Inability to film in Kenya, causing catastrophic schedule and budget disruption.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Finalize all stunt sequences and secure the required IATSE-certified stunt coordinator, safety officer, and medical personnel. Their availability may be limited.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Inability to film stunt sequences, significant safety liability, and insurance invalidation.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Develop a comprehensive welfare plan for all child performers, including scheduling tutors and a certified welfare officer. Submit plan to regulatory bodies for approval.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Legal violations, fines, and potential revocation of child work permits.

complianceRecommendations.recommendation: Structure the initial schedule draft to minimize weekend work and night shoots to provide a baseline budget before adding costly scenes.
complianceRecommendations.impactIfIgnored: Initial budget estimates may be unrealistically low, leading to financial strain later in production.

riskAssessment.description: Delays in processing Kenyan work permits for key cast or crew.
riskAssessment.impact: Shooting schedule delayed, key personnel unable to work, potential need to recast or re-crew locally at high cost.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Submit all applications 45-60 days in advance, not the 21-day minimum. Engage an experienced local fixer to manage the process.

riskAssessment.description: Injury to a stunt performer during a high-risk sequence.
riskAssessment.impact: Immediate production halt, medical emergency, potential legal and insurance investigation, long-term schedule delays.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Strict adherence to all safety protocols, including mandatory rehearsals, personnel certification, and on-site medical teams. Do not deviate from approved stunt plan.

riskAssessment.description: Systematic schedule overruns leading to cascading overtime and meal penalties.
riskAssessment.impact: Significant budget overspend on labor costs, potentially compromising funds for other departments.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Build a 10% contingency into daily shooting schedules. Track work hours in real-time and have ADs flag potential overtime situations 2 hours in advance.

riskAssessment.description: An unintentional violation of child performer work/rest/education rules.
riskAssessment.impact: Immediate production halt by welfare officer or regulator, fines, negative press, and potential loss of permit to work with minors.
riskAssessment.mitigation: The welfare officer's schedule and time-tracking is paramount and must override the AD's shooting schedule. The welfare officer must sign off on the daily call sheet for all minors.

nextStepRecommendations: Provide detailed cast and crew list with union categories for specific rule application.
Submit scene breakdown with estimated times, locations, and special requirements (stunts, animals, children, makeup).
Submit a proposed shooting schedule for a full compliance audit against this ruleset.
